יִהְיוּ takes the recasting have with its subject pronoun under rule 43's first sentence, since הָיָה is what makes the clause possessive; the ASV's he does not agree in number with the plural verb, but it is the pronoun that is written.
בִּגְדֵי־קֹדֶשׁ הֵם follows rule 20: the copula are joins the predicate noun and the explicit pronoun הֵם takes only they.
in water leaves the assimilated article unrepresented (rules 12, 29), while the construct nouns of the anarthrous chains (כְּתֹנֶת, מִכְנְסֵי, אַבְנֵט, מִצְנֶפֶת) each take a supplied the.
